slides.headline: Serving all summer? Your forearm noticed
slides.sub: Where remedial massage fits for tennis players, and where it doesn't.

slides.title: Where tennis players tighten up
slides.body: Grip loads the forearm and wrist, serving loads the back of the shoulder, footwork loads the calves and quads, and every stroke rotates the mid-back. These are common areas a remedial massage therapist works on.

slides.title: What massage can help with
slides.body: Many players find massage helps them feel looser, eases that heavy-arm feeling after a big week and makes moving more comfortable. The effects are usually short-term, so treat it as support rather than the whole plan.

slides.title: Timing around your matches
slides.body: A lighter session a day or two before a tournament usually suits, with deeper work once the weekend is done. Avoid trying a deep session for the first time the day before a big match.

slides.title: Pair it with strength work
slides.body: Massage complements rehab rather than replacing it. Forearm strengthening, rotator cuff exercises and calf raises build the capacity tennis asks for, so your body copes with more hitting.

slides.title: When to see a physio first
slides.body: Elbow pain lingering for weeks, shoulder pain that wakes you at night, or a sudden sharp pain in the calf mid-rally are worth a physio assessment before booking a massage.

slides.headline: Book a post-tennis tune-up
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy work alongside our physios, so hands-on care fits into a bigger plan for your game. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Serving all summer? Your forearm, shoulder and calves have probably noticed. 🎾

Tennis loads the same areas again and again: grip through the forearm, serving through the back of the shoulder, stop-start footwork through the calves and quads. Remedial massage can help those areas feel looser and ease the heavy-arm feeling after a big week.

It's usually a short-term effect, so it works well alongside strength work for the forearm, shoulder and calves rather than instead of it. Keep lighter sessions close to match days and deeper work for after.

Lingering elbow pain, night shoulder pain or a sudden calf pain mid-rally are worth a physio check first. Book online via the link in bio.

story.body: Between sets, open and close your hand 20 times and gently stretch your wrist. Massage helps; strength work keeps you hitting.
